subject: Design: federated pilot dataflow, EU routing & no-model-learn toggles
messages:
From: Paul Carter <paul.carter@greenoakhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@greenoakhealth.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scope + dataflow questions (EU residency + no-learning)

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the GreenOak product team and our privacy folks liked the latency profile. Before we spin up the pilot we need to lock a few operational items in the DPA and runbook:

- EU residency requirement: all request-level inputs (chat prompts, form submissions) must be processed and persisted only in EU-hosted nodes for EU tenants.
- No-model-learning opt-out: GreenOak requires an explicit no-model-learning commitment for EU tenant data (no training, no tuning, no derivative model updates).
- Prompt/response IP: GreenOak expects customer prompts and generated responses to remain their data; Redwood must confirm whether any derivative IP could be asserted by the platform.

Attached is a hand-drawn dataflow and a DPA redline from our counsel (DPA-GreenOak-v3.docx). Can you confirm how the private routing + on-prem / VPC options map to a "no-model-learning" toggle? Also: what artifacts (audit logs, attestation) can we provide to prove no training occurred?

Paul
Paul Carter
Head of Integrations, GreenOak Health
paul.carter@greenoakhealth.com

Attachments: goh-dataflow-diagram.pdf (diagram), DPA-GreenOak-v3.docx (redline)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Carter <paul.carter@greenoakhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + dataflow questions (EU residency + no-learning)

Paul — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Summary answers below; we should schedule a short sync with your legal team for the DPA redlines.

1) EU routing & residency
- We can pin the pilot to EU-hosted capacity (Frankfurt primary, Amsterdam failover). All request processing, ephemeral KV cache, and logs for the pilot tenant will remain in those regions.
- For additional assurance we provide an on-demand export of the request logs and a region-specific audit report (S3 export to your SFTP) on a weekly cadence.

2) No-model-learning opt-out
- We offer a per-tenant "no_model_learning" flag at provisioning. When enabled:
  - No telemetry or request content is forwarded to model improvement pipelines.
  - Inference traces used for runtime optimization (latency histograms, token counts) are aggregated and anonymized; request text is excluded.
  - We can provide an attestation signed by our security team plus delivery of runtime logs showing the flag was active.

3) Prompt/response IP and derivatives
- Contractually we confirm that user-provided prompts and generated responses remain the customer's data for the scope of the pilot; Redwood will not assert ownership of prompt/response content or derivatives for data covered by the no_model_learning flag.
- We treat model weights and baseline model derivative outputs differently (standard platform models remain Redwood property) — the DPA clause will specify the customer content carveout.

Next steps: 1) Karthik and I will draft language for the DPA to add an explicit per-tenant no-learn covenant + audit artifacts, 2) share the DPA draft link, 3) quick legal sync. When works for you next week?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + dataflow questions (EU residency + no-learning)

Paul / Marissa — quick technical follow-up and commit points from infra: 

- Implementation: we'll enforce the no_model_learning flag at the routing layer. When set, requests are served by a tenant-isolated inference pool; telemetry hooks that normally copy request text to model improvement stores are turned off.
- Evidence: we can provide the following artifacts for the pilot:
  1) Tenant provisioning record showing the flag was set (timestamped).
  2) Server-side config snapshot (sha256) for the runtime cluster during the pilot.
  3) A weekly CSV export of audit events (no request payloads) plus a signed attestation from Security.
- Edge case: if GreenOak requests failover to non-EU capacity during a regional outage, we will notify and require explicit approval before routing out of the EU. We can also configure auto-failover off for the pilot.

I'll start a draft DPA paragraph and an operational checklist we can push into the pilot runbook. Marissa — can you add Ben from Legal Ops to the thread? He can help with audit artifact formats.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Product, Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick legal-ops note here. For the DPA redline we want to: 

- Add a short clause: "No Model Learning: For customer tenants with the no_model_learning flag enabled, Redwood will not use request content for model training, tuning, or derivative model creation." Keep it scoped to the pilot duration and tenant ids.
- Add an evidence appendix template: what we'll hand over on request (signed attestation, config snapshot, CSV audit events, and SFTP path if they want exports).
- Export controls: include a paragraph that if GreenOak requests periodic SFTP exports of EU-resident request logs, Redwood will deliver a sanitized set (no PII beyond what GreenOak requests).

I'll prep a DPA snippet and attach to the HubSpot record. Marissa — I'll also draft the short attestation template so Security can sign during the pilot.

Ben
